exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs vaginal delivery)
infant feeding method (breastfeeding vs formula feeding)
outcome: incidence of gastrointestinal disorders (regurgitation, colic, constipation)
cohort: 82 newborns born at term and their mothers.
finding: Cesarean section was associated with a higher incidence of regurgitation in infants, while formula feeding and antibiotic therapy were linked to an increased risk of atopic dermatitis by 12 months of age.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a higher incidence of regurgitation in infants.
